questions.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
questions.description:
You are given a collection of intervals. Merge all overlapping intervals and return the resulting set of non-overlapping intervals.

### Input
The first line contains a single integer `n`, the number of intervals. Each of the next `n` lines contains two space-separated integers `start end` (`start <= end`) describing one interval. The intervals are **not** given in any particular order.

### Output
Print the merged intervals as `start end`, one per line, sorted in ascending order by `start`. If `n` is `0`, print nothing (the expected output is the empty string).

### Merging rule
Two intervals overlap if they share any point *or merely touch* — `[1, 3]` and `[3, 5]` are considered overlapping and must be merged into `1 5`. Only a strict gap (the next interval's `start` is greater than the current merged interval's `end`) starts a new group.

### Worked example
Input (given out of order):
```
3
1 3
6 8
2 5
```
Sorted by start this is `[1, 3]`, `[2, 5]`, `[6, 8]`. `[1, 3]` and `[2, 5]` overlap (2 <= 3), merging into `[1, 5]`. `[6, 8]` does not overlap `[1, 5]` (6 > 5), so it stays separate.

Output:
```
1 5
6 8
```

testCases.description: normal unsorted input with one overlap and one separate interval
one interval fully contained inside another
no overlaps at all, given out of order
negative coordinates with an overlap and a separate interval
larger input, 10 intervals unsorted with several merge groups
